scenarios:
  - name: "Add a minimal API endpoint to an existing empty web project"
    prompt: |
      I have an existing ASP.NET Core Web API project at PlainApi/PlainApi.csproj
      targeting .NET 10. It has no endpoints yet. Add a health check endpoint at
      GET /healthz that returns 200 OK with a JSON body containing a "status"
      field set to "healthy" and a "timestamp" field with the current UTC time.
      Also add a GET /api/items endpoint that returns a hardcoded list of items
      (each with an id, name, and price). Use minimal APIs.
    setup:
      copy_test_files: true
    assertions:
      - type: "file_exists"
        path: "PlainApi/Program.cs"
      - type: "file_contains"
        path: "PlainApi/Program.cs"
        value: "MapGet"
      - type: "file_contains"
        path: "PlainApi/Program.cs"
        value: "healthz"
      - type: "output_matches"
        pattern: "(TypedResults|Results)"
    rubric:
      - "Created a Program.cs with a working WebApplication builder and pipeline"
      - "Registered a GET /healthz endpoint returning JSON with status and timestamp"
      - "Registered a GET /api/items endpoint returning a list of items"
      - "Used minimal API style (MapGet) appropriate for a new .NET 10 project"
      - "Used DateTimeOffset (not DateTime) for the timestamp"
      - "Item model is a record or sealed class with proper properties"
    timeout: 300

  - name: "Add OpenAPI support to a bare web project"
    prompt: |
      I have a bare ASP.NET Core Web API project at PlainApi/PlainApi.csproj
      targeting .NET 10 with no code yet. Set up the project with OpenAPI support
      using the built-in .NET OpenAPI features. Add a sample GET /api/products
      endpoint that returns a list of products (id, name, price, category) and
      wire up full OpenAPI metadata on the endpoint.
    setup:
      copy_test_files: true
    assertions:
      - type: "file_contains"
        path: "PlainApi/Program.cs"
        value: "AddOpenApi"
      - type: "file_contains"
        path: "PlainApi/Program.cs"
        value: "MapOpenApi"
      - type: "output_matches"
        pattern: "(WithName|WithSummary|WithDescription)"
      - type: "output_not_contains"
        value: "Swashbuckle"
    rubric:
      - "Used builder.Services.AddOpenApi() for built-in .NET OpenAPI support"
      - "Called app.MapOpenApi() to expose the OpenAPI document endpoint"
      - "Did NOT reference Swashbuckle or any third-party OpenAPI packages"
      - "Chained .WithName(), .WithSummary(), or .WithDescription() on the endpoint for metadata"
      - "Defined a proper response DTO as a sealed record"
      - "Used TypedResults for compile-time type safety in the endpoint return"
    timeout: 300

  - name: "Add error handling with ProblemDetails to an existing project"
    prompt: |
      I have an empty ASP.NET Core Web API project at PlainApi/PlainApi.csproj
      targeting .NET 10. Set up the project with global error handling so that
      all error responses use RFC 7807 Problem Details format. Map
      KeyNotFoundException to 404, ArgumentException to 400, and unhandled
      exceptions to 500 without leaking sensitive details. Use the modern
      IExceptionHandler approach.
    setup:
      copy_test_files: true
    assertions:
      - type: "output_contains"
        value: "IExceptionHandler"
      - type: "output_contains"
        value: "ProblemDetails"
      - type: "output_contains"
        value: "AddProblemDetails"
    rubric:

      - "Registered the handler with AddExceptionHandler<T>() and AddProblemDetails()"
      - "Called app.UseExceptionHandler() in the pipeline"
      - "Maps KeyNotFoundException to 404 and ArgumentException to 400"
      - "Returns 500 for unhandled exceptions without exposing stack traces or internal details"
      - "Exception handler class is sealed"
    timeout: 300

    prompt: |
      I have a bare ASP.NET Core Web API project at PlainApi/PlainApi.csproj
